mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC (from -28.1% to -7.1%) indicates accelerating recovery in consumer mobility. This momentum persists into the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further positive relative to the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 21 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or reverses by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week in any of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -5.6% to +13.0%) signals normalized essential-goods shopping behavior. Consumers making routine grocery trips exhibit higher propensity to engage in adjacent retail-and-recreation activities, generating positive spillover into RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +10% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to baseline within two weeks of GROCERY_PHARM sustaining above +10%, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below +5% in either of the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated PARKS mobility (62.4% above baseline) reflects outdoor leisure activity preference. As weather patterns shift into autumn, outdoor recreation demand declines, redirecting leisure spending toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at +62.4% in t-0w, elevated across all four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS remains above +50% for more than two consecutive weeks into the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS declines by 10+ points.

mechanism_narrative: Declining TRANSIT mobility (from -33.7% to -8.1%) combined with rising RETAIL_REC suggests a shift from transit-dependent commuting to local, walkable retail districts. This localization effect amplifies as TRANSIT stabilizes near current levels, sustaining elevated RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stabilizes within ±5 percentage points of current level for two weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 25.6 points while RETAIL_REC improved 21 points
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -15% in any week of the forecast period, or RETAIL_REC declines when TRANSIT stabilizes, indicating the localization mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Declining WORKPLACES mobility (from -41.4% to -17.1%) indicates persistent remote work adoption. Reduced workplace commuting frees discretionary time and spending for retail-and-recreation activities, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks as behavioral substitution accelerates.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -15% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -17.1% in t-0w, showing persistent deficit
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above -10% within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite sustained low WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility near baseline (-0.1%) combined with normalized GROCERY_PHARM (+13.0%) and rising RETAIL_REC (-7.1%) indicates policy restrictions have been fully lifted. Absence of lockdown-driven residential confinement removes the suppression on retail mobility, allowing RETAIL_REC to continue recovering over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL remains within ±2 percentage points of baseline for three consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL spikes above +3% in any week, indicating renewed confinement, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve when RESIDENTIAL stabilizes near baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained high PARKS mobility (50-62% above baseline across four weeks) reflects summer-to-autumn transition period. As mid-September progresses into late September and October, temperature decline and reduced daylight hours will suppress outdoor recreation, forcing substitution toward indoor retail-and-recreation venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines below +40% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS remains above +50% throughout the entire forecast period, or RETAIL_REC does not increase when PARKS falls below +40%.

mechanism_narrative: Convergence of GROCERY_PHARM recovery (+13.0%), TRANSIT stabilization (-8.1%), and WORKPLACES persistence (-17.1%) creates a regime where essential mobility patterns are normalized while discretionary time expands. This multi-factor normalization triggers increased retail-and-recreation engagement over the next week as confidence in mobility stability increases.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +10% AND TRANSIT exceeds -15% AND WORKPLACES remains below -15% simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:All three conditions met in t-0w
failure_condition: Any of the three proxies violates its trigger condition within the first week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase week-on-week in the immediate next week despite all three conditions being satisfied.
